Ctrl K AI & Vectors AI & Vectors The best vector database is the database you already have. Supabase provides an open source toolkit for developing AI applications using Postgres and pgvector. Use the Supabase client libraries to store, index, and query your vector embeddings at scale. The toolkit includes: A vector store and embeddings support using Postgres and pgvector. A Python client for managing unstructured embeddings. An embedding generation process using open source models directly in Edge Functions. Database migrations for managing structured embeddings. Integrations with all popular AI providers, such as OpenAI , Hugging Face , LangChain , and more. Search # You can use Supabase to build different types of search features for your app, including: Semantic search : search by meaning rather than exact keywords Keyword search : search by words or phrases Hybrid search : combine semantic search with keyword search Examples # Check out all of the AI templates and examples in our GitHub repository. Headless Vector Search A toolkit to perform vector similarity search on your knowledge base embeddings. Image Search with OpenAI CLIP Implement image search with the OpenAI CLIP Model and Supabase Vector. Hugging Face inference Generate image captions using Hugging Face. OpenAI completions Generate GPT text completions using OpenAI in Edge Functions. Building ChatGPT Plugins Use Supabase as a Retrieval Store for your ChatGPT plugin. Vector search with Next.js and OpenAI Learn how to build a ChatGPT-style doc search powered by Next.js, OpenAI, and Supabase. Integrations # OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company. Supabase provides a way to use OpenAI in
your applications. Amazon Bedrock A fully managed service that offers a choice of high-performing foundation models from
leading AI companies. Hugging Face Hugging Face is an open-source provider of NLP technologies. Supabase provides a way to use
Hugging Face's models in your applications. LangChain LangChain is a language-agnostic, open-source, and self-hosted API for text translation,
summarization, and sentiment analysis. LlamaIndex LlamaIndex is a data framework for your LLM applications. Case studies # Berri AI Boosts Productivity by Migrating from AWS RDS to Supabase with pgvector Learn how Berri AI overcame challenges with self-hosting their vector database on AWS RDS
and successfully migrated to Supabase. Firecrawl switches from Pinecone to Supabase for Postgres vector embeddings How Firecrawl boosts efficiency and accuracy of chat powered search for documentation using

zh.summary: 把 Postgres、身份认证和应用后端合在一起，为 AI 开发工具提供可部署的数据底座。
zh.judgment: 优势在从生成原型到持久化业务数据的短路径；生产权限、费用和迁移决定长期价值。
zh.replaces: 开发者分别搭数据库、登录、文件存储和接口，再给 AI 原型补后端。
zh.product: 官网与文档提供数据库、认证、存储、实时订阅和边缘函数，并用 pgvector 支持向量检索。它是 AI 应用的基础设施，不是通用对话产品；功能状态在官网逐项标注。
zh.customer: 开发者、AI 应用构建平台和企业后端团队是明确对象。平台可把后端随生成的应用一起配置；付费触发更可能是上线、用量及团队治理需求，而非第一次成功生成页面。
zh.workflow: 文档说明创建项目后存储业务数据与嵌入向量，用权限策略控制访问，再通过客户端与函数接到应用。可研究的交付是带身份边界的运行后端，不能把能查询向量当成完整 RAG 质量验证。
zh.business_model: 核验价目列出免费层、Pro 每月 25 美元起、Team 每月 599 美元起及定制企业层，另计计算与超额用量。月费不是整个应用的总成本，多个项目、流量与日志会改变账单。
zh.traction: 官网有 Lovable 等客户案例，说明后端可嵌入生成应用的流程。案例及规模数字属于公司发布，未独立核对；项目创建数不能代替活跃付费项目与续费。
zh.moat: 与自己维护 Postgres 和多个服务相比，集成与开发体验有价值；与其他托管后端相比，迁移能力和可靠治理更关键。业务数据、运维惯性与平台分发可能形成持续性，向量功能本身容易被复制。
zh.funding_read: 融资可支持容量与开发生态，但资本事件不是数据库业务盈利的证明。应验证生成工具带来的项目，在上线后有多少持续使用并覆盖计算与支持成本。
zh.risks: 错误权限策略可能暴露用户数据，用量增长也可能放大成本。原型快速上线若省略备份、迁移和恢复，可能把获客速度换成未来服务负担。
zh.takeaway: 把原型所缺的持久化、认证和权限连成默认路径。以可迁移的业务数据降低接入顾虑，同时让上线后的费用和责任清楚可见。
zh.watch_next: 看生成项目到生产项目的转化、活跃付费项目、计算利用率和恢复表现。将免费尝鲜与真正承载业务的项目分组，才能评估分发渠道的商业质量。

en.summary: A Postgres development platform joining database, authentication and backend services for AI-built applications.
en.judgment: The wedge is the path from generated prototype to durable data; permissions, cost and migration determine lasting value.
en.replaces: Assembling a database, authentication, storage and APIs separately after generating a prototype.
en.product: Official product material covers Postgres, authentication, storage, realtime and edge functions. The AI guide adds pgvector retrieval. This is application infrastructure, with individual feature maturity labels, rather than a general conversational assistant.
en.customer: Developers, AI app-building platforms and enterprise backend teams are identifiable users. Deployment, usage and team governance are plausible payment triggers; generating one working screen is not equivalent to production demand.
en.workflow: The documented path creates a project, stores application data and embeddings, applies access policies, then connects clients and functions. A running permission-aware backend is the output; vector retrieval alone does not validate an entire RAG system.
en.business_model: The reviewed page lists Free, Pro from $25/month, Team from $599/month and custom Enterprise, plus compute and overages. Plan fees are not total application cost: extra projects, traffic and logging affect bills.
en.traction: Official Lovable and other customer stories show integration into app-generation workflows. Case and scale claims remain company-published. Created projects do not establish active paid deployments or retention.
en.moat: Integration and developer experience differentiate it from self-managed Postgres plus separate services. Against managed-backend rivals, portable data and dependable governance matter more than vector search alone.
en.funding_read: Capital may support capacity and ecosystem expansion without establishing profitable database operations. Watch whether generated projects become continuing production workloads that cover infrastructure and support costs.
en.risks: Incorrect access policies can expose data, while growing usage can increase bills. Skipping backups, migration and recovery during rapid prototyping can create later service obligations.
en.takeaway: Make persistence, authentication and permissions a default completion path for prototypes. Portable data reduces adoption friction; explicit operating costs make production decisions clearer.
en.watch_next: Watch prototype-to-production conversion, active paid projects, compute utilization and recovery. Separate free experiments from applications carrying recurring business workloads.
